title: I made an UNO-inspired roguelike with AI, and the free Steam demo is out now
author: id187
selftext:
I've just released the free Steam demo for Match & Ruin, a single-player card roguelike I'm making in Godot.

It starts with the familiar idea of matching cards, but you control three mercenaries with separate hands. You match ranks or suits using ordinary playing cards, and the card you play changes what the next mercenary can use to attack, defend or activate a skill. You can also win by forcing the enemy over its hand limit.

I came up with the basic game concept and designed the monsters' traits and mechanics myself. AI helped me implement those designs in the game.

I also used AI to brainstorm relic ideas and compose music. It helped me come up with ways to use underused mechanics and create relics and trinkets around them. Beyond the initial design, I used AI across most of the development, including programming, artwork, writing and localization. Everything is prepared content; nothing is generated during play.

The demo includes six mercenaries to play and unlock, and goes through the first chapter into the middle of chapter two. It's free on Steam for Windows:

[https://store.steampowered.com/app/5310800/Match\_\_Ruin\_Demo/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5310800/Match__Ruin_Demo/)

If you try it, I'd like to hear whether planning across the three hands feels clear in the first few battles. I'm also happy to talk about how I used AI during development.

comments.author: flex_sculpting
comments.body:
This looks like an awesome twist on the genre!
Managing three separate hands using standard card ranks/suits sounds like it adds a ton of tactical depth, especially with that hand limit win conditions
